description: A 2nd BCE chariot burial that appears to have become a focus of religious activity during the Roman period. Cattle remains recovered from the enclosing ditch were dated between the late 1st - early 4th CE and are thought to represent religious activity. A nearby square post-hole and beam-slot structure was thought to possibly represent a related shrine, but is poorly dated.
bibliography: Brown, Fraser. The Archaeology of the A1 (M): Darrington to Dishforth DBFO Road Scheme. Oxford Archaeology North, 2007.
